title: THREE WORLDS, ONE FACT
goal: One fact can support more than one world.

steps.action: Keep the event fixed.
Invent three models for why it happened.
Each model must predict a different thing you could observe next.
Notice the earliest observation that would separate them.
Until that evidence arrives, speak in plurals: possibilities, not prophecy.

win: ✓ Possibilities plural. Prophecy cancelled.
supports: Exhale after “Speak Plurals”; leave the forecast.
I can use “Invent” while fear stays loud.
formula_flow: Keep Event → Invent → Predict Different → Earliest → Speak Plurals
safety:
PAUSE
Do not multiply theories when an urgent practical response is already clear.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ADD THE PREFIX
goal: Grammar can turn a fact back into an event.

steps.action: Take the exact thought and place these words before it: ‘I am noticing my mind produce…’ Say the complete sentence once at ordinary speed.
Notice what remains true and what loses command authority.
Carry on with the next chosen task while the sentence exists nearby.

win: ✓ Urgency lost its shortcut to the decision.
supports: Exhale after “Resume Task”; slow the clock.
I can use “Check Command” without rushing.
formula_flow: Prefix Thought → Check Command → Resume Task
safety:
PAUSE
Drop the wording if it feels mocking, unreal, or destabilising.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THANKS, MIND. NO CONTRACT.
goal: Protection can be acknowledged without being hired.

steps.action: Ask what danger the thought is trying to prevent.
Offer a precise thank-you for that intention.
Then answer: ‘I’m not signing this instruction.’ Choose a matching what matters to you action that keeps any useful caution but rejects the controlling move.
Respect the alarm; decline the contract.

win: ✓ I thanked the alarm for trying to protect me—and declined its contract.
supports: I can use “Thank Intention” while pain stays real.
formula_flow: Ask Danger → Thank Intention → Answer M → Respect
safety:
PAUSE
Do not dismiss warnings that point to concrete and immediate danger.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THOUGHT DEPARTURES
goal: Give thought transport, not a throne.

steps.action: Place the thought on something already moving: a bus passing, a leaf in drainage water, subtitles leaving a screen.
Watch its full arrival and departure without pushing it faster.
When the carrier exits, return your eyes to one stationary object.
Another vehicle may come; none owns the station.

win: ✓ Let the thought pass without giving it the station.
supports: Exhale after “Allow Departure”; loosen the label.
I can use “Watch Arrival” without becoming the label.
formula_flow: Place Thought → Watch Arrival → Return Eyes → Allow Departure
safety:
PAUSE
Stop imagery if it increases detachment from surroundings.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: NAME THE SERIES
goal: This episode has aired before.

steps.action: Ignore today’s plot for ten seconds.
Ask what recurring series it belongs to: ‘The Rejection prediction,’ ‘Everyone Is Ahead,’ ‘I Must Fix It Now.’ Give the series a short title and season number.
Then check if this episode contains new information or recycled footage.

win: ✓ Someone else’s position stopped defining mine.
supports: Exhale after “Ask Whether”; drop the scoreboard.
I can use “Ask Recurring” without ranking my worth.
formula_flow: Ignore → Ask Recurring → Ask Whether
safety:
PAUSE
Retire any title that ridicules genuine pain or identity.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: COMMAND DOWNGRADE
goal: Turn the order into a weather report.

steps.action: Hear the command exactly as it arrives: ‘Leave now,’ ‘Check again,’ ‘You must reply.’
Remove the command tone and turn it into an observation: ‘An urge to leave is here,’ ‘An urge to check is here,’ or ‘An urge to reply is here.’
Let the urge give you information without giving it authority.

win: ✓ Wanting became a signal instead of an instruction.
supports: Exhale after “Reject Authority”; let wanting crest.
I can use “Downgrade It” without obeying the urge.
formula_flow: Picture Command → Reject Authority
safety:
PAUSE
Act immediately when the original command reflects genuine safety needs.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PASSENGER THOUGHT
goal: You do not need an empty vehicle to steer.

steps.action: Choose one two-minute action that matters.
Invite the thought to ride in the passenger seat—audible, uncomfortable, unedited.
Hold hands on the action wheel and complete the movement while it talks.
At the destination, notice who actually drove.

win: ✓ Thought stayed in the passenger seat. Steering remained mine.
supports: Exhale after “Who Drove?”; slow the clock.
I can use “Ride Passenger” without rushing.
formula_flow: Choose Time → Ride Passenger → Keep Hands → Who Drove?
safety:
PAUSE
Shorten the trip if functioning or situational awareness drops.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MAKE A WIDER CONTAINER
goal: Capacity grows sideways, not through force.

steps.action: Locate the unwanted sensation.
Find its edges.
Soften the muscles around—not inside—it.
Include one neutral body area and one external sound in awareness.
You are enlarging the room, not evicting the guest.

win: ✓ Made more room around the feeling instead of trying to evict it.
supports: Exhale after “Widen the Room”; keep the compass.
I can use “Find Edges” while pain stays real.
formula_flow: Locate Unwanted → Find Edges → Soften Muscles → Include Neutral → Widen the Room
safety:
PAUSE
Stop and orient outward if expansion produces flooding or feeling unreal or disconnected.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PAIN PLUS THE FIGHT
goal: Separate the wound from the fist wrapped around it.

steps.action: Imagine two lanes: WHAT HURTS and WHAT RESISTANCE ADDS.
In the first lane, picture the raw sensation or fact.
In the second lane, name demands, self-attack, bracing, and impossible arguments with reality.
Release one item from the resistance lane while respecting the hurt.

win: ✓ Hurt stayed respected while one layer of fighting came off.
supports: Exhale after “Drop One Fight”; release extra blame.
“Catch The Fight” keeps blame in proportion.
Look back: “Make Two Lanes” → “Drop One Fight”.
I can use “Keep The Hurt” without owning everything.
formula_flow: Make Two Lanes → Keep The Hurt → Catch The Fight → Drop One Fight
safety:
PAUSE
Do not use acceptance language to tolerate abuse, injustice, or untreated symptoms.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CAMERA FIRST, CAPTION SECOND
goal: Experience arrives before the commentary team.

steps.action: For fifteen seconds, collect camera data: colour, movement, sound, pressure, position.
Then say the event using only that footage.
Now add the meaning separately and label it CAPTION.
Keep both; never confuse their sources.

win: ✓ Camera and caption separated. Neither gets to impersonate the other.
supports: Exhale after “Keep Sources”; leave the forecast.
I can use “Describe Event” while fear stays loud.
formula_flow: Camera Mode → Describe Event → Add Caption → Keep Sources
safety:
PAUSE
Switch to safety action when the facts themselves show immediate risk.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ENTER THE ACTION
goal: Stop watching yourself do the thing; do the thing.

steps.action: Choose one ordinary activity.
Place vision, touch, posture, and hearing inside it.
When attention leaves, re-enter through the next physical contact point rather than scolding yourself.
Stay until the activity reaches its natural edge.
Participation, not perfect focus, is the target.

win: ✓ Action got there before perfect focus.
supports: Exhale after “Enter Fully”; release the score.
I can use “Place Vision” without perfecting.
formula_flow: Choose Ordinary → Place Vision → Leave Re → Stay Activity → Enter Fully
safety:
PAUSE
Do not narrow attention during driving, caregiving, or tasks requiring broad awareness.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE ATTENTION BOUNCER
goal: Not every thought gets the same access to your attention.

steps.action: Notice the next thought without following it.
Stamp it REQUESTED, RELEVANT, or UNINVITED.
Give only the chosen category a short timer; let the others wait without argument.
When the timer ends, return to the task or deliberately admit one new thought.

win: ✓ The mental pile-up has a front edge again.
supports: One exhale after “Return Door”; redirect attention.
I can use “Stamp Access” amid noise.
formula_flow: Spot Arrival → Stamp Access → Set Budget → Return Door
safety:
PAUSE
Stop if the labels become a checking ritual or make urgent action harder.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: EMOTION, COMPLETE YOUR ARC
goal: Feelings move differently when they are not put on trial.

steps.action: Locate the emotion in the body and give it a precise name.
Permit its current intensity without feeding the story.
Track where sensation travels, peaks, breaks, or cools.
Follow until one natural shift appears, then choose the action the situation—not the wave—requires.

win: ✓ The wave moved through; the situation was still there to choose from.
supports: Gently exhale after “Follow Appears”; no forcing.
I can use “Permit” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Locate Emotion → Permit → Track Sensation → Follow Appears
safety:
PAUSE
Seek help for escalating self-harm, aggression, panic, or inability to function.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ONE CLEAN WISH
goal: Goodwill can interrupt hostility without pretending closeness.

steps.action: Bring the person to mind at a safe distance.
Choose one honest wish that does not deny harm: ‘May we both be free from causing more suffering,’ or ‘May safety become possible.’ Offer it once.
Then state the boundary or action you still need.
Warmth does not cancel discernment.

win: ✓ Warmth stayed intact without making discernment disappear.
supports: Exhale after “Keep Discernment”; release extra load.
I can use “Keep It Honest” without carrying it all.
formula_flow: Bring Person → Keep It Honest → State Boundary → Keep Discernment
safety:
PAUSE
Do not direct compassion exercises toward an abuser if it weakens necessary distance.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE 2% SOFTENING
goal: Your face can send the body a quieter memo.

steps.action: Without forcing happiness, release the forehead, loosen the eyes, and lift the mouth corners by only two percent.
Keep the expression believable.
Hold it while looking at one neutral object.
Ask whether defence changed by even half a notch.

win: ✓ Half a notch was enough to prove defence can soften.
supports: Gently exhale after “Ask Whether”; no breath-holding.
I can use “Keep Expression” while alarm rises.
formula_flow: Release Forehead → Keep Expression → Hold Neutral → Ask Whether
safety:
PAUSE
Skip this if smiling feels unsafe, invalidating, painful, or socially risky.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PLAY THE BODY PASSWORD
goal: A short body code can prove that alarm has not taken every control.

steps.action: Choose three tiny comfortable movements, such as tap a knee, touch a thumb, and look at one fixed object. Say the order once.
do A–B–C slowly, pausing after each movement long enough to feel it finish.
do C–B–A at the same pace. If you lose the order, return to neutral and restart instead of speeding up.
Name the movement you directed most clearly, then let the whole code stop.

win: ✓ The body surge lost some of its authority.
supports: Gently exhale after “Claim Control”; no breath-holding.
I can use “Run Order” while alarm rises.
formula_flow: Set Code → Run Order → Reverse Code → Claim Control
safety:
PAUSE
Do not play while driving, moving through hazards, dizzy, injured, or unable to stay oriented.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE FOUR-LETTER BRAKE
goal: Crisis speed must pass four gates before action.

steps.action: S — stop every nonessential movement.
T — take one physical step back.
O — observe facts, sensations, and the strongest impulse.
P — proceed with the smallest safe move that will still make sense in an hour.
Do not negotiate with momentum between letters.

win: ✓ Four letters bought enough time to interrupt momentum.
supports: Exhale after “Skip Negotiation”; let wanting crest.
I can use “Take Physical” without obeying the urge.
formula_flow: Stop Nonessential → Take Physical → Observe Facts → Proceed Safely → Skip Negotiation
safety:
PAUSE
Use emergency support when immediate danger cannot be managed by a pause.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ONE FOOT HERE, ONE FOOT NEAR IT
goal: Hold distress and safety in the same frame.

steps.action: Choose a stable anchor such as feet on the floor or a fixed sound.
Keep most attention there while allowing a small edge of distress into awareness.
Verify the anchor remains present.
Adjust the ratio until both can coexist without losing choice.

win: ✓ The memory moved one step back toward then.
supports: Gently exhale after “Tune the Ratio”; orient to now.
“Choose Stable” to “Tune the Ratio”: what loosened?
I can use “Keep Most” while staying in now.
formula_flow: Choose Stable → Keep Most → Anchor Verify → Tune the Ratio
safety:
PAUSE
Increase anchoring or stop if distress takes the whole field.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: EXHALE IN CHAPTERS
goal: A large release can become several manageable ones.

steps.action: Instead of one continuous out-breath, let air leave in three soft portions with tiny unforced spaces between.
Keep the face loose and never push to empty.
After the final segment, wait for the body’s next inhale rather than grabbing it.

win: ✓ The narrative stopped owning every room.
supports: Exhale after “Wait Body”; then keep moving.
I can use “Keep Face” before motivation.
formula_flow: Let Air → Keep Face → Wait Body
safety:
PAUSE
Resume normal breathing if segmentation causes urgency or tingling.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: LET THE FIELD SELF-PUBLISH
goal: Observe experience without appointing a headline.

steps.action: Open Field with sight, sound, sensation, and thought available at once.
Notice whatever becomes prominent, then what replaces it.
Do not select, rank, or hold any item.
Track the changing editorial order for one minute.

win: ✓ A belief moved from law to hypothesis.
supports: Exhale after “Track the Shift”; loosen the label.
I can use “Whatever” without becoming the label.
formula_flow: Open Field → Whatever → Let All Arrive → Track the Shift
safety:
PAUSE
Open monitoring should stop if unstructured awareness feels overwhelming.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: NO FAVOURITE SENSATION
goal: Receive what arrives without keeping or ejecting it.

steps.action: Let the field choose its next foreground.
Pleasant, unpleasant, dull, or vivid—offer each the same brief hospitality.
When preference reaches to grip or reject, include that movement too.
End by noticing the whole room at once.

win: ✓ A physical signal lost its automatic meaning.
supports: Exhale after “End Whole”; leave the forecast.
I can use “Pleasant” while fear stays loud.
formula_flow: Let Field → Pleasant → Include Movement → End Whole
safety:
PAUSE
Use a stable anchor instead during high body alarm or feeling unreal or disconnected.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE SENSE ROLL CALL
goal: Make the present answer in specifics.

steps.action: Find five distinct colours or shapes, four contact sensations, three separate sounds, two scents, and one taste or mouth sensation.
No generic answers; ‘blue attention’ beats ‘something blue.’ Let the inventory end with the most stable item.

win: ✓ Five senses checked in; one steady detail got the last word.
supports: Exhale after “Answer Blue”; notice the room.
I can use “Answer Blue” to return here.
formula_flow: Find Five → Answer Blue
safety:
PAUSE
Adapt counts or omit channels that are unavailable or triggering.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: EXPAND–GATHER–EXPAND
goal: Move awareness through an hourglass.

steps.action: First, acknowledge the full weather of the moment.
Next, gather attention around breathing as a small centre.
Finally, widen to the whole body and surrounding space.
Spend roughly one minute in each shape.
Carry the final wide frame into your next movement.

win: ✓ There is space between the mind and what it produced.
supports: Gently exhale after “Carry Final”; no forcing.
I can use “Breathe Small” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Acknowledge → Breathe Small → Widen Whole → Spend → Carry Final
safety:
PAUSE
Use a non-breath anchor if respiration is activating.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: RAIN WITHOUT THE UMBRELLA
goal: Meet the experience before trying to change the prediction.

steps.action: Recognise what is here.
Allow this moment of it to exist.
Investigate with one kind question about body or need.
Notice that the experience is present but not the whole of you.
Move through R–A–I–N once; resolution is not a required fifth letter.

win: ✓ The experience was met without making resolution a requirement.
supports: Gently exhale after “Move R”; no forcing.
I can use “Allow Moment” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Recognise → Allow Moment → Question About → Experience → Move R
safety:
PAUSE
Skip investigation when acute distress requires stabilisation first.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: FOUR PARTS OF ONE STEP
goal: Walking can become a moving attention track.

steps.action: Slow enough to separate lift, travel, place, and weight transfer.
Follow those four events through several steps.
When thought pulls away, rejoin at whichever phase the foot is currently performing.
Finish by walking normally while retaining one point of contact.

win: ✓ Walking stayed ordinary while attention stayed connected.
supports: One exhale after “Finish Walking”; redirect attention.
I can use “Follow Events” amid noise.
formula_flow: Place Weight → Follow Events → Thought → Finish Walking
safety:
PAUSE
Practise only where slowed walking is physically safe.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: LISTEN PAST THE SOUND
goal: The disappearance is part of the Notice.

steps.action: Ring, play, or notice a safe sustained sound.
Follow its decay with precision until you cannot locate any remainder.
Stay with the silence that receives it, not with memory of the tone.
Let the next surroundings sound end the practice.

win: ✓ The sound stopped owning the whole moment.
supports: Exhale after “Let Surroundings”; leave the forecast.
I can use “Follow Decay” while fear stays loud.
formula_flow: Play Safe → Follow Decay → Stay Silence → Let Surroundings
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid intense volume or tones associated with distress.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: NOTICE THE NOTICING
goal: Turn attention toward the fact that experience is known.

steps.action: Choose any sensation.
First recognise its qualities.
Then ask, without answering verbally, ‘How is this already known?’ Rest with the immediacy of knowing rather than searching for an object called awareness.
Return by naming one visible fact.

win: ✓ Awareness noticed itself—then landed back on one visible fact.
supports: One exhale after “Return Fact”; redirect attention.
formula_flow: Choose Sensation → Recognise → Ask Verbally → Return Fact
safety:
PAUSE
Discontinue if self-referential attention increases unreality.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE BREATH HINGE
goal: Rest where one phase becomes another.

steps.action: Follow a natural inhale to the instant it turns toward exhale.
Do not hold or stretch the hinge.
Notice the same effortless change at the bottom of exhalation.
Visit each threshold lightly, then allow several breaths to pass unwatched.

win: ✓ Starting became smaller than the story around starting.
supports: Exhale after “Allow Breaths”; then keep moving.
I can use “Leave Hinge Free” before motivation.
formula_flow: Follow Inhale → Leave Hinge Free → Change → Allow Breaths
safety:
PAUSE
Leave the hinge alone if waiting creates retention or air hunger.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WHERE SOUND BECOMES HEARING
goal: Trace vibration to its inner arrival point.

steps.action: Listen to a sustained, gentle sound.
Follow it from apparent distance toward the place where it becomes an auditory experience—ear, head, body, or nowhere locatable.
When the border between outside vibration and inside hearing blurs, rest there briefly.

win: ✓ Sound lost its border for a moment; hearing became the event.
supports: Gently exhale after “Rest Briefly”; no forcing.
I can use “Follow Apparent” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Listen Sustained → Follow Apparent → Rest Briefly
safety:
PAUSE
Choose ordinary grounding if auditory focus feels intrusive or voice-like.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: BORROW THE SKY’S WIDTH
goal: Let vision teach attention another size.

steps.action: Gaze softly into open sky or another unobstructed safe field.
Release pinpoint focus and include the edges of vision.
Without forcing calm, compare the width outside with the contraction inside.
Allow attention to occupy both.

win: ✓ The view widened enough for thought and sky to coexist.
supports: One exhale after “Keep Wide View”; redirect attention.
“Open Sky” to “Keep Wide View”: what loosened?
I can use “Release Pinpoint” amid noise.
formula_flow: Open Sky → Release Pinpoint → Compare Width → Keep Wide View
safety:
PAUSE
Never sky-gaze while driving or in unsafe light and weather.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE BODY AS INNER SPACE
goal: Trade the sense of a solid block for a more spacious inner map.

steps.action: Imagine the torso and limbs as volumes containing room rather than dense objects.
Notice cavities, distances, and open intervals inside the body inner picture while maintaining feet, seat, and external orientation in space.
Keep the image gentle and anatomically nonliteral.

win: ✓ The body image became more spacious without needing to become literal.
supports: Exhale after “Keep Image”; notice the room.
I can use “Cavities” to return here.
formula_flow: Imagine Torso → Cavities → Keep Image
safety:
PAUSE
Stop immediately if the exercise makes you feel unreal, disconnected, numb, or less oriented to the room.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CATCH WANTING BEFORE THE OBJECT
goal: Desire starts moving before it names a destination.

steps.action: Wait at the first pull: leaning, brightening, reaching, mental zoom.
For five seconds, observe wanting as raw movement without completing ‘I want…’.
Only afterward name the object and decide whether pursuit serves the wider situation.

win: ✓ Wanting and doing are separate again.
supports: Exhale after “Name Object”; leave the forecast.
I can use “Observe Wanting” while fear stays loud.
formula_flow: Wait Pull → Observe Wanting → Name Object
safety:
PAUSE
Use added support for dangerous cravings or impaired control.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WATCH PLEASURE LEAVE CLEANLY
goal: The ending of pleasantness is not a failure.

steps.action: Choose a mild enjoyable sensation.
Track its rise, fullness, thinning, and the eventual return to neutral.
Resist grabbing for a second dose during the fading phase.
Notice what remains when the pleasant signal is gone.

win: ✓ Pleasure ended cleanly without turning the ending into a problem.
supports: Exhale after “Let Pleasure Leave”; leave the forecast.
“Choose Mild” to “Let Pleasure Leave”: what loosened?
I can use “Track Rise” while fear stays loud.
formula_flow: Choose Mild → Track Rise → Resist → Let Pleasure Leave
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid using this to restrict nourishment or healthy enjoyment.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: NOT FOR, NOT AGAINST
goal: Release both hands of mental grasping.

steps.action: Notice whether experience is being pulled closer or pushed away.
Relax the corresponding inner movement without demanding neutrality.
Let the content remain unowned and unobstructed for a short interval.
Then act according to circumstance, not attraction or aversion.

win: ✓ Rejection became an event, not an identity.
supports: Exhale after “Act According”; drop the scoreboard.
“Act According”: what changed from “Check The Pull”?
I can use “Relax” without ranking my worth.
formula_flow: Check The Pull → Relax → Let Content → Act According
safety:
PAUSE
Do not release practical action needed to protect health, rights, or safety.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: STAY AT THE SENSE DOOR
goal: What you notice can occur without being kidnapped by the object.

steps.action: Choose one sound or sight.
Notice the first sensory contact, then keep attention at the doorway of hearing or seeing rather than following associations outward.
When the mind travels to the object’s story, return to bare contact.

win: ✓ Story dropped away; bare sensation was enough.
supports: Exhale after “Return Bare”; notice the room.
I can use “Sensory” to return here.
formula_flow: Choose Sound → Sensory → Return Bare
safety:
PAUSE
Keep awareness broad during tasks that require surroundings monitoring.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WHO RECEIVED THAT THOUGHT?
goal: Turn inquiry toward the assumed owner.

steps.action: When a thought appears, ask ‘To whom did this occur?’ If ‘me’ arises, ask ‘What is this me before the answer?’ Refuse biography, role, body description, and philosophy.
Stay with the question’s open edge for several heartbeats.

win: ✓ The label stayed readable without staying absolute.
supports: Exhale after “Hold Question”; loosen the label.
I can use “Hold Question” without becoming the label.
formula_flow: Ask Whom → Hold Question
safety:
PAUSE
Return to concrete sense of where you are if inquiry feels ungrounding.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: REMOVE THE NAME BADGES
goal: See what remains when roles clock out briefly.

steps.action: Name the roles active today. Keep the pace deliberately slow here.
One by one, imagine placing each badge on a table—parent, worker, partner, achiever, patient, helper.
Sit without using any badge to answer ‘Who am I now?’ After a short pause, reclaim only the role needed next.

win: ✓ I took the name badges off and noticed I was still here.
supports: Exhale after “Release Roles”; leave the forecast.
I can use “Imagine Badge” while fear stays loud.
formula_flow: Name → Imagine Badge → Release Roles
safety:
PAUSE
Keep grounding and avoid role stripping if identity feels fragile.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PUT THE FEELINGS BACK IN ORDER
goal: Feelings that seem tangled may be answering different moments.

steps.action: Name up to three present feelings. Do not explain them yet.
Which arrived first? Put it at the left of a short line.
Add the concrete cue that each feeling answered—words heard, an image, a body change, or a later thought.
Read the sequence once: ‘First ___ answered ___; then ___ answered ___.’ Stop after the order is clear.

win: ✓ The tangle became a sequence. Each feeling got its own moment.
supports: Exhale after “Read Order”; let wanting crest.
I can use “Find First” without obeying the urge.
formula_flow: Name Mix → Find First → Link Cue → Read Order
safety:
PAUSE
Stop if sequencing pulls you into flashback, self-blame, numbness, or forced certainty about the past.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE THREE QUALITIES WEATHER REPORT
goal: Mental states are climates, not surnames.

steps.action: Sort the current movement as clarity, agitation, inertia, or a mixture.
Notice its speed, energy, and attentional style.
Choose the smallest balancing condition—rest for agitation, body alarm for inertia, protection for clarity.
Recheck later without saying ‘I am this.’

win: ✓ I read the inner weather without turning it into an identity.
supports: Exhale after “Say Recheck”; then keep moving.
formula_flow: Classify → Speed → Choose Smallest → Say Recheck
safety:
PAUSE
Use clinical assessment where agitation or inertia may reflect a serious condition.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE SIX-LINK FIRE CHAIN
goal: Anger often begins several stations before the explosion.

steps.action: Trace the sequence backward: confusion or loss of judgement; anger; frustrated desire; attachment; repeated attention; original cue.
Find the earliest link still reachable now. Use the simplest true sentence you can.
Remove fuel there—shift attention, loosen attachment, or revise the demand.

win: ✓ I found one link feeding the fire and removed fuel there.
supports: Exhale after “Remove Fuel”; soften the jaw.
I can use “Earliest” without extra heat.
formula_flow: Trace Sequence → Earliest → Remove Fuel
safety:
PAUSE
Create distance; obtain help whenever aggression or violence risk is present.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: DO NOT REPLACE THE LAST THOUGHT
goal: Silence often disappears because the mind fills it immediately.

steps.action: Wait for a thought to end naturally.
At the first empty beat, resist generating commentary about emptiness.
Rest for the duration available—even a fraction.
Let the next thought arise without invitation.
Count the gap only after it is over.

win: ✓ What matters stayed reachable inside the loss.
supports: Exhale after “Count Gap”; keep the compass.
I can use “Empty” while pain stays real.
formula_flow: Wait Thought → Empty → Rest Duration → Let Thought → Count Gap
safety:
PAUSE
Use external engagement if silence feels frightening or destabilising.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PAY FOR THE NEXT LAP
goal: Another lap costs minutes of your actual life.

steps.action: Name the exact question you want one more thinking lap to answer. One sentence only.
Choose what those three minutes will replace: rest, a message, food, movement, work, or a decision. Say the trade plainly.
If the trade is worth it, set three minutes and think only about the named question. If not, close the lap now.
When the clock ends, stop without buying another lap. Do the displaced activity or deliberately let it go.

win: ✓ Toll paid once. No second lap purchased.
supports: Exhale after “Close Toll”; end the lap.
I can use “Price Trade” without another lap.
formula_flow: Name Lap → Price Trade → Buy Three → Close Toll
safety:
PAUSE
Never buy another analysis lap with sleep, medication, food, immediate safety, or time-critical responsibilities.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: IMAGINE THE FEELING’S SHAPE
goal: Visual form can hold what words flatten.

steps.action: Without aiming for beauty, assign the state a colour, texture, shape, size, and position in your mind.
Add a boundary, pressure source, and possible exit route.
Change one visual property and notice whether the inner state shifts.

win: ✓ I changed the feeling’s shape and watched the inner state answer back.
supports: Exhale after “Change One Feature”; release extra load.
I can use “Add Boundary” without carrying it all.
formula_flow: Assign Colour → Add Boundary → Change One Feature
safety:
PAUSE
Stop if imagery becomes graphic, compulsive, or more disturbing.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PUT THE MEMORY BACK IN PAST TENSE
goal: Grammar can accidentally keep history live.

steps.action: Retell one short segment using was, happened, had, and then.
After every emotionally loaded sentence, insert three present facts: your present location, the current year, and what choice exists now.
Finish with: ‘That ended; this moment is different.’

win: ✓ The sentence moved the memory back into past tense.
supports: Exhale after “Finish Moment”; let feeling settle.
I can use “Ground Between” while emotion stays loud.
formula_flow: Use Happened → Ground Between → Finish Moment
safety:
PAUSE
Do not retell alone if the memory overwhelms sense of where you are.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THREE SELVES, THREE JOBS
goal: Present-you should not do every time period’s labour.

steps.action: Picture three time zones: PAST, PRESENT, FUTURE.
Place completed actions in PAST, available repair in PRESENT, and prevention plans in FUTURE.
Move any item that belongs to the wrong time zone.
do only one PRESENT task now.

win: ✓ Present-me did present-me’s job and stopped carrying the other two shifts.
supports: Exhale after “Do Present Job”; end the lap.
At “Do Present Job”, compare “Make Time Zones”.
I can use “Complete Actions” without another lap.
formula_flow: Make Time Zones → Complete Actions → Reassign → Do Present Job
safety:
PAUSE
Do not use time ownership to evade current accountability for earlier harm.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PUT THE YEARS BACK BETWEEN THEM
goal: Put the real years back between then and now.

steps.action: Picture the dates of the events that currently feel piled together.
Give equal physical space to equal spans of time; do not place every event in one crowded cluster.
Notice TODAY at the correct distance and name one fact that belongs only to now.
Look again at the oldest event and rate how immediate it feels after the spacing is restored.

win: ✓ Speed stopped masquerading as necessity.
supports: Exhale after “Recheck Urgency”; slow the clock.
I can use “Scale Distance” without rushing.
formula_flow: Date Events → Scale Distance → Present → Recheck Urgency
safety:
PAUSE
Stop and reorient to the room if the timeline makes the past feel more present.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: DELETE ‘AM’ FROM THE SENTENCE
goal: Identity verbs can turn weather into a prison.

steps.action: Restate ‘I am broken/lazy/anxious’ without am or is.
Use temporary action language: ‘Avoiding has increased this week,’ ‘Anxiety is moving through the chest,’ ‘Energy dropped after…’.
Add one condition under which the process changes.

win: ✓ The emotion became evidence to consider, not evidence that decides.
supports: Exhale after “Add Condition”; let feeling settle.
I can use “Use Temporary” while emotion stays loud.
formula_flow: Drop Identity Verb → Use Temporary → Add Condition
safety:
PAUSE
Keep diagnostic terms where clinically useful; remove only overgeneralised identity.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THIRD-PERSON OWNERSHIP TEST
goal: Grammar can loosen the grip without denying the experience.

steps.action: Frame the moment once as ‘this mind is predicting…’ or ‘the system is producing…’.
Notice what changes in intensity, responsibility, and choice.
Then return to first person for the action you really own: ‘I will…’.
Distance the content, not agency.

win: ✓ I loosened the grammar without giving away ownership of the experience.
supports: Exhale after “Loosen the Grammar”; end the lap.
I can use “Change” without another lap.
formula_flow: Describe Event → Change → Return Person → Loosen the Grammar
safety:
PAUSE
Stop if altered pronouns increase estrangement from self.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ZOOM LENS TRAINING
goal: Attention needs more than one focal length.

steps.action: Select an object.
Spend ten seconds on one tiny feature, ten on the object and nearby context, and ten on the whole visual field.
Repeat in reverse.
Select the aperture that best fits the actual task.

win: ✓ I changed focal length instead of forcing one kind of attention to do every job.
supports: Exhale after “Select Aperture”; keep both sides.
formula_flow: Choose Object → Spend → Repeat Shift → Select Aperture
safety:
PAUSE
Use broad awareness in environments that require hazard monitoring.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE PRICE OF KEEPING THIS SELF
goal: Every identity grants permissions and charges fees.

steps.action: Imagine three buckets: IT LETS ME; IT STOPS ME; IT DEMANDS FROM ME.
Mentally sort the self-concept into those three buckets.
Focus on the highest hidden cost and ask whether the identity still earns its keep.

win: ✓ Thought stopped earning time simply by returning.
supports: Exhale after “Find The Price”; end the lap.
“Fill The Buckets” proves loops can stop.
Difference check: “Sort Identity Costs” → “Find The Price”.
I can use “Fill The Buckets” without another lap.
formula_flow: Sort Identity Costs → Fill The Buckets → Find The Price
safety:
PAUSE
Preserve identities that provide community, protection, or meaning unless change is genuinely chosen.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CALL THE INNER COUNCIL
goal: Conflicting parts need coordination, not forced unanimity.

steps.action: Give each self-state a seat.
One sentence each: what I need, what I fear, what I propose.
Appoint a chair whose job is to protect the whole system over time.
The chair may combine, delay, or reject proposals, but must acknowledge every need.

win: ✓ Every inner voice got heard; none got automatic control.
supports: Exhale after “Chair the Council”; end the lap.
“Give Self” versus “Chair the Council”: what eased?
I can use “Sentence” without another lap.
formula_flow: Give Self → Sentence → Protect Whole → Chair the Council
safety:
PAUSE
Use professional support if parts feel autonomous, dangerous, or disorganising.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ADD THE WITNESS WHO SHOULD HAVE BEEN THERE
goal: The remembered self deserves credible rethought.

steps.action: Introduce a compassionate observer appropriate to the event—a trusted adult, advocate, elder, clinician, or current-you.
Have them name what was wrong, what protection was deserved, and what is true about the person who endured it.
Keep their words believable.

win: ✓ The missing witness finally sounded believable, not magical.
supports: Exhale after “Keep It Believable”; watch the thought.
I can use “Name Wrong” without obeying thought.
formula_flow: Introduce → Name Wrong → Keep It Believable
safety:
PAUSE
Use guided trauma work if imagined witnessing intensifies grief or flashback.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: RELATIONSHIP DATA, NOT ONE BIG FEELING
goal: Separate episodes before declaring the pattern.

steps.action: For recent interactions, hold event, context, frequency, repair attempt, and outcome as separate mental snapshots. Let your weight settle into the chair or floor.
Look for repetition and exceptions.
Issue a narrow conclusion tied to the observed period rather than ‘always’ or ‘never.’

win: ✓ The relationship stopped collapsing into one giant feeling.
supports: Exhale after “Issue Narrow”; keep both sides.
I can use “Look Repetition” before concluding.
formula_flow: Hold Event → Look Repetition → Issue Narrow
safety:
PAUSE
Do not use data collection to remain in an unsafe relationship.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: APOLOGY NEEDS THREE EVIDENCE POINTS
goal: A real apology leaves evidence, not just a tone.

steps.action: Define what adequate repair requires: clear acknowledgement, changed action, and prevention of return.
Specify what evidence would show each over time.
Check the apology against those criteria rather than immediate emotion.

win: ✓ The apology had to produce evidence before emotion could approve it.
supports: I can use “Specify” while emotion stays loud.
formula_flow: Return Define → Specify → Evaluate
safety:
PAUSE
No repair test obliges renewed contact after serious harm.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: SET THE CONTACT DOSE
goal: Closeness can be realistic instead of accepted or abandoned completely.

steps.action: Before contact, choose frequency, duration, permitted topics, location, and exit phrase.
Start with the lowest dose that preserves both connection and regulation.
Review afterward using body and behaviour, not guilt.

win: ✓ I set a dose of contact my body and behaviour can actually review.
supports: Exhale after “Use Body”; keep both sides.
I can use “Start Lowest” before concluding.
formula_flow: Choose Frequency → Start Lowest → Use Body
safety:
PAUSE
Reduce or end contact when boundaries are ignored or safety is compromised.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WHAT SPECIES OF UNKNOWN IS THIS?
goal: Different uncertainties require different responses.

steps.action: Categorise the unknown: answerable now, answerable later, influenceable but unknowable, or permanently unknowable.
Apply its matching move—research, schedule, act on influence, or practise acceptance.
Refuse to use one category’s tool on another.

win: ✓ The unknown got a species name—and finally received the right tool.
supports: Exhale after “Use Category”; leave it unanswered.
I can use “Apply Move” without a guarantee.
formula_flow: Classify → Apply Move → Use Category
safety:
PAUSE
Reclassify when access to information or influence changes.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PLAN BOTH BRANCHES
goal: Uncertainty need not prevent preparation.

steps.action: Choose two plausible outcomes and build a short branch for each: first signal, first action, resource, and exit.
Prepare any step useful in both branches now.
Delay preference until evidence selects the path.

win: ✓ Both futures got a plan before either one earned belief.
supports: Exhale after “Select Path”; leave it unanswered.
I can use “Prepare Both” without a guarantee.
formula_flow: Choose Plausible → Prepare Both → Select Path
safety:
PAUSE
Add branches only when they are genuinely plausible and decision-relevant.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.
